terms.definition: The unit plugins are distributed in: an npm, git or local package containing one or more plugins.
The decision whether a tool call runs. How it is made depends on the approval mode: auto, ask or full.
A point where the agent's view of a session folds to its memory, the files it read back and a handoff.
The menu after `/`.
Where the user writes: the draft area and the model line under it.
A plugin's public schemas and service tags, which other plugins and its own parts depend on.
An input that takes the composer's place when the app needs a decision from the user, built by a tool or flow that offers options, such as approval, questions, trust and commit.
An overlay for browsing and picking from a list the user opened.
One saved record in a session's log, such as a message, a tool call, a notice or a checkpoint.
The note the agent writes at a checkpoint: the request, unfinished work and the next action.
Markdown rules an agent reads only when doing the work they cover.
Summaries Liminal writes of a session so the agent keeps working after a checkpoint: long-term and short-term.
A list of choices opening above the composer while the user types.
One package that adds a capability to Liminal, in parts: manifest, contract, server and TUI.
What the user types in the composer and submits.
Applying changed plugin code to the running app at the end of a turn.
One conversation with the agent, kept as an ordered log of entries.
The menu after `@`.
A named action the agent can call, such as `read` or `edit`, with a description and parameters.
One use of a tool by the agent, with its result.
A user's decision that a folder's project plugins and instructions may load.
One run of the agent, from the user's input until it stops replying.
The project's agreed terms, kept in `.liminal/vocabulary.json`.
